rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The righteous recline on thrones and behold God's favors and grandeur, in contrast to wrongdoers barred from their Lord; they will also see their enemies' fate.
rows.anchor: witness the favour and blessings of God

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The freshness and bloom on the faces of the righteous visibly reflect the favors surrounding them.
rows.anchor: freshness and bloom that reflects on the faces of those who are engulfed with favours from all sides

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pure wine offered to the righteous will be sealed with musk and opened for them.
rows.anchor: This wine will be sealed with

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The description gives only a general idea of the wine; striving to drink it rebukes those who spend all their effort seeking transient worldly pleasures.
rows.anchor: Only those people will have an idea of its actual taste and characteristics who will get the opportunity to drink it

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word mazaaj denotes a liquid mixed with wine to heighten or moderate its effects.
rows.anchor: refers to a liquid which is mixed with alcohol to increase its serene effects

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The accusative aynan is specification, while biha is locative; the favored wine is properly drunk beside a river, unlike worldly wine consumed wherever available.
rows.anchor: The word !ًْﻋﻴﻨﺎ is declined in the accusative because of specification

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He rejects the common rendering of bi as ‘from it’ as vague and redundant, preferring its customary locative sense because Tasnim has already been named as the source.
rows.anchor: Our exegetes have not been able to determine the true connotation of the particle ب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Drinking pure wine on a river bank has its own etiquette, unlike the wretched wine of this world.
rows.anchor: The most appropriate place to drink wine is on a river bank

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The scene reverses worldly fortunes when the deeds of sinners and righteous are judged, recalling how arrogant rich people mistreated poor Muslims.
rows.anchor: This is a portrayal of the reversal of situation which will take place when the results of the deeds of the sinners and the righteous will be declared

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The furtive winking may describe believers passing the arrogant leaders, or the Quraysh leaders passing the Muslims and signaling one another to humiliate them.
rows.anchor: This can refer both to the fact that when these believers passed by them or when the arrogant leaders of the Quraysh passed by the Muslims

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After harassing believers, the wrongdoers return to their families boasting as though they had achieved success, exposing their meanness rather than shame.
rows.anchor: they return engrossed as if they had achieved some great success

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers act cautiously around family so their conduct does not mislead others toward ruin; the mischief-makers instead boast of their pranks to teach the next generation evil.
rows.anchor: they would always spend their lives among their family in

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Quraysh leaders tried to suppress positive reactions to believers by calling them astray and portraying their belief in the Hereafter as hostility to ancestral religion.
rows.anchor: The arrogant leadership of the Quraysh

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Many people were moved by Muslims' deep belief in the Hereafter, so Quraysh countered by labeling them irreligious and deeply misguided.
rows.anchor: many people were positively influenced by seeing the deep roots

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He reads the statement that the Muslims were not appointed guardians as part of the disbelievers' own taunt: they objected that Muslims criticized their deeds without authority to reform them.
rows.anchor: In my opinion, this sentence is actually a part of the words

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Judgment reverses the worldly mockery: believers will laugh at disbelievers justly, since truth left them no excuse and they still treated believers as criminals.
rows.anchor: in this world, it was the disbelievers who would laugh at the believers; but on that day, it would be the other way round

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: From their thrones the believers will see God's blessings and look into Hell to witness the disbelievers' fate, even questioning them as described elsewhere.
rows.anchor: they would also while sitting there be able to peep

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question about the disbelievers being duly repaid seeks confirmation from the believers and includes the earlier mistreatment of them.
rows.anchor: After receiving all these favours, the believers

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The heavens and earth will be annihilated before the new world's different physical laws begin; the upheaval cannot now be imagined and will destroy even the proud people's strongest structures.
rows.anchor: The new world which will be created after the Day of Judgement

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adhinat means that the sky listened and obeyed; haqqat means its obedience is essential and befitting because God created it.
rows.anchor: he accepted what he said; he obeyed his directive

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse admonishes conceited people who argue at every point: the sky will obey its Lord, so how can a tiny human under it claim otherwise?
rows.anchor: This sentence is meant to admonish and instruct these

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The flattened earth will cast out what lies hidden in it, especially the dead, but the general wording includes everything buried there, including the affluent's treasures.
rows.anchor: on that day, this earth will be stretched out like a sheet of cloth and it will expel whatever is hidden in its folds

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The image suggests the burdened earth will feel relief when it sheds its contents, as a pregnant woman does after childbirth.
rows.anchor: the earth is burdened with all these things just as a pregnant woman is burdened with the child she is carrying

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Both sky and earth will willingly obey God on that Day, as stated in another Qur'anic passage.
rows.anchor: It shows that both the sky and the ea rth will obey their Lord

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Though humanity is addressed generally, the warning particularly targets conceited people absorbed in worldly life, who are inevitably being drawn to meet their Lord.
rows.anchor: Although the address of this sūrah is general

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kadh means to strive with great labor; human life is an unbroken journey from birth through changing stages and conditions to death, regardless of status.
rows.anchor: to make an effort in something with great labour.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Meeting the Lord is the purpose of life's journey: people must be held accountable, the objective for which this world was created.
rows.anchor: The purpose of this meeting is obviously to hold them accountable for their deeds

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A right-hand record and easy reckoning indicate salvation: good deeds outweigh evil deeds, so minor blemishes are forgiven; those whose evil deeds predominate face account for each deed and punishment.
rows.anchor: guarantee enough for making them entitled to salvation

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God will unite believers in Paradise with believing family members of lower rank by raising the family's status rather than lowering theirs.
rows.anchor: He will in fact upgrade the status of their family

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers' joy at reunion reflects concern for their family's Hereafter, unlike people heedless of it; the author contrasts the latter's worldly rejoicing with believers' fear for family and God's rescue.
rows.anchor: about their family achieving success in the Hereafter than in this world

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: True love of family requires concern for their Hereafter and encouraging that concern; indifference will doom both and turn reunion into mutual cursing.
rows.anchor: The real requirement of the love a person has for his family is that he should be concerned for their well-being in the Hereafter

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The record is handed from behind, with a contextual implication that it is in the left hand; another sūrah states the left-hand detail explicitly.
rows.anchor: there is no mention of the fact that their account will be handed over to them in their left hands, yet there is a strong contextual indication to this

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The group faces two humiliations: a record in the left hand and delivery from behind; further reflection suggests their hands are tied behind them like criminals.
rows.anchor: this group will face two humiliations at the same time

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The doomed group longs for death on entering Hell, but death will not relieve its torment; the effect is placed before its cause to sharpen the contrast with believers' reunion.
rows.anchor: to make the discourse more forceful, the effect has been placed before the cause

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They lose the joy of family reunion because they spent worldly life unconcerned about their own or their relatives' Hereafter; enjoying future favors requires sacrifice.
rows.anchor: It is essential that a person has made the requisite sacrifice if

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They assumed they would not be raised after death and therefore pursued worldly pleasure without concern for the Hereafter, where they expect no share.
rows.anchor: The implication is that they thought that after their death

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's watching over people refutes their denial of return: He will call them to Him, consistently with His power, wisdom, justice and mercy; this is used elsewhere as an argument for Judgment.
rows.anchor: The fact is that their Lord is watching over them

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The three oaths substantiate the claim that people will meet their Lord; their destination is certain, though reached gradually, as all things reach culmination gradually under God's practice.
rows.anchor: The muqsam ‘alayh of these oaths is verse 19: you shall certainly ascend gradually

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: La before the oath is neither redundant nor denial of the oath; it preemptively refutes the audience's false claim, a natural rhetorical style also found in other languages.
rows.anchor: this particle is neither superfluous nor is it meant to refute the oath

rows.speaker: Lexicographers
rows.claim: Lexicographers explain what the night gathers as the things it collects or encloses.
rows.anchor: Lexicographers explain it by saying

rows.claim: Most exegetes take the gathered things to be animals that seek shelter at night.

have regarded this to refer

rows.speaker: Some exegetes
rows.claim: Some other exegetes take the gathered things to be rivers, mountains and trees hidden by the night.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He prefers stars: they are closely associated with night and their commanded appearance, movement and setting show God's control, supporting humanity's journey to Him.
rows.anchor: For this reason, to me this refers to the stars

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The moon is singled out as a specific example after the general reference to heavenly bodies; its waxing and waning directly illustrates the gradual journey toward God.
rows.anchor: is a mention of the specific after the general

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The expression tasqa means when the moon grows into a full moon.
rows.anchor: means when the moon grows into a full moon

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The moon must follow its gradual path and descend after reaching fullness; like it and other celestial bodies, people inevitably progress through stages toward God and should not deny the Hereafter because they cannot demand a glimpse.
rows.anchor: His journey may be gradual – a practice of God found in all phenomena of nature

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Given the clear signs, the disbelievers' failure to believe in the Hereafter and in reward and punishment is astonishing.
rows.anchor: they must have really lost their senses if after all these blatant signs they are not professing faith in the Hereafter

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When the Qur'an announces this great truth, prostration should express gratitude for its greatness and news; their arrogant denial reverses that proper response.
rows.anchor: it was only befitting for them to have

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arabs and Egyptians would prostrate to acknowledge impressive discourse; the author cites Pharaoh's magicians and poets who prostrated on hearing Labid as examples.
rows.anchor: Here worth considering the fact is a tradition of the Arabs

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disbelievers rejected the Qur'an outright, claiming it was fabricated to frighten them about the Hereafter.
rows.anchor: has been fabricated by the person who is presenting it

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows all they amass: wealth, deeds and their consequences; immediate worldly gains blind them, and they will understand the reality only in the Hereafter.
rows.anchor: The immediate gains of this world have led them to this attitude

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If people enslaved to worldly love refuse the Qur'anic path, the Prophet should warn them of deserved torment; only faith and righteous deeds bring salvation and eternal reward.
rows.anchor: Only those people will be saved from this torment

none: closing formula and publication date only

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sūrah al-Humazah counters al-ʿAṣr: instead of urging truth and steadfastness, the miserly hoard wealth and taunt people who urge others to fulfill God's and fellow people's rights, hoping to demoralize them.
rows.anchor: reveals a clear similarity in their themes

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Miserliness and wealth hoarding recur elsewhere in the Qur'an; 9:79 condemns those who censure believers' generous giving and mock poor givers.
rows.anchor: people who greedily hoard money

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mutatawwi and mutatawwa describe someone who fulfills obligations and eagerly performs optional acts beyond them.
rows.anchor: only fulfils his obligations but also enjoys doing what is optional

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lamz means to censure, slander or speak ill of someone.
rows.anchor: to censure, to slander, to speak ill of

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cited verse describes hypocrites who neither give in God's cause nor tolerate seeing others give.
rows.anchor: the hypocrites do not spend in the cause of God and also cannot bear to see others doing so
